rites.name: Thanulde
rites.text: Thanulde is the concept of the first sounding in Torugun, the Singing that condensed the roots of the world out of silence. It is understood as a rising note that bound loose matter into the first stable ground.

rites.name: Sereoliarus
rites.text: Sereoliarus is a concept of Torugun, the discipline by which Courtsworn measure a challenger's resolve before a council of judges. It is less a weapon than a standard, a bearing that makes a held line hold and a sworn word bind.

rites.name: Osunareno
rites.text: Osunareno is a concept of rhythm and tempo in Torugun, born in the Courts during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between worlds. It is said to measure the pulse that held the doors between realms in place, and its presence steadied councils and trials alike.

rites.name: Torukar
rites.text: Torukar is a stone-bound warden of the Martial realm, a quiet guardian whose authority runs through the ground beneath every fortress in Torugun. Its witnessed power is modest: it hurls falling boulders from the heavens and wraps its charge in a sphere of living granite. Elders of the realm agree it is the least of its kind, yet its steady presence has never once been broken.

rites.name: Thazhourkun
rites.text: Thazhourkun is a sentient ember-lattice that drifts through the cooling crust of Torugun, weaving hot seams into stone to shape new mountain ranges. Its kind sings low tones to guide magma veins toward the surface where settlers harvest the warmth.

rites.name: Graithokoth
rites.text: Graithokoth is a sealed doctrine of storm-bearing vows in the Martial realm of Torugun, held by a circle of duelists who swear their breath into iron. Its bearers can draw the pressure of the high air into arcs of white fire and thin, unbroken beams of light. Its greatest rite calls a towering, sky-bodied servant out of the cloud to hurl lightning on command.

rites.name: Khaggok
rites.text: Khaggok is a ritual war-engine of the Martial realm, a hulking iron gong-warden that marks the seventh age of Torugun's battle-schools. It channels pressure through its bronze plating to hurl shattering concussive pulses that can split a fortress wall in a single strike.

rites.name: Vhaigoth
rites.text: Vhaigoth is a sealed-away resonance engine that hums only when a worthy champion overcomes a guardian within the Torugun marshes. Each triumph grants the wielder a new discipline of motion or strength, though the discipline must be relearned each time the engine cools.

rites.name: Grouthok
rites.text: Grouthok is a veil-technique of the Martial realm in Torugun, taught to rival blade-dancers who wish to strike unseen. The practitioner's form fades from the sight of foes for a brief span, though a shadow lingers and blows still land true. Its extended form lets the user slip past watchers far longer, at the cost of greater stillness.

rites.name: Drouthok
rites.text: Drouthok is a thirsty war-engine of the Martial realm in Torugun, a brass-ribbed colossus that drinks the rain of storm-fronts to power its fists. In the seventh age of its making it learned to fold the distance between two fighters' stations, letting a warrior stride to either their own citadel or the rival's by a tap or a long hold.

rites.name: Gukar
rites.text: Gukar is a martial spinning technique of the Torugun powers, a whirlwind unleashed after a foe falls, letting the wielder spin far longer and faster than ordinary practitioners. Its adepts use the gyre to glide across chasms and to slice through hazards that would otherwise harm them. Among the dojo masters, the style is said to echo the rising wail of a storm before it reaches its peak.

rites.name: Vorukougurn
rites.text: Vorukougurn is a second-skin aerial discipline in Torugun, a martial art where a fighter's momentum is re-spun mid-air by a coil of rune-wrapped bone at the spine. Practitioners can reverse their fall once more than gravity allows, and masters have been known to vault clean over a fortress wall.

rites.name: Druggurn
rites.text: Druggurn is a sealed war-engine of the Martial realm, a brass-ribbed amplifier that gathers a warrior's blows and multiplies their force fourfold for a single breath. Its wardens use it sparingly, since the engine drinks the wielder's own stored vigor to fuel each surge.

rites.name: Voraithak
rites.text: Voraithak is a rhythmic thrust-art drawn from the pulsing dance of the ember-moths of Torugun's high cliffs. Practitioners compress their own heartbeat into a sudden vertical surge that carries them skyward and shatters any brittle barrier they strike, though reinforced alloys resist it entirely.

rites.name: Grougok
rites.text: Grougok is a fabled pair of soft-soled boots worn by the wardens of the Hollow Vaults of Torugun, who must cross trembling bridges of volatile crystal without setting them off. The boots grant a slow, deliberate gait, but the wearer must never halt mid-crossing, or the charges beneath their feet will erupt.

rites.name: Thagar
rites.text: Thagar is a Martial-realm enhancement called the Quickening Stride, a pair of tireless ember-lined boots that let a wearer sprint far faster than their natural gait while still gathering scattered tokens of power along the way. Its bearers are said to gain the ability only after overcoming a final champion of their trial. Warriors across the Torugun march value it chiefly for letting the wearer reach fallen prizes before rivals can.

rites.name: Krokuzhurn
rites.text: Krokuzhurn is a sentient gravity-anchor of the Martial realm, a stonewalled fortress-spirit that hurls its own weight downward in a single crushing descent. It is said to have sealed three rebel valleys during the Sundering Age, and its stillness is regarded as the most dangerous thing in Torugun.

rites.name: Gurnok
rites.text: Gurnok is a seismic war-chant of the Torugun drumlands, a rhythmic stomp that awakens buried fault lines beneath the battlefield. Its bearers are said to hammer the earth until mountains split along old seams and ridgelines crumble into dust.

rites.name: Karozhuthun
rites.text: Karozhuthun is a martial technique of the Torugun realm, practised by wandering duelists who rotate their bodies in tight rhythmic bursts to build momentum. Its final form, the three-turn surge, lets a practitioner spin thrice and dart across a field at a blur, leaving a trail of displaced air. It was sealed away after a famous tournament and is taught only to those who prove their timing.

rites.name: Thisseth
rites.text: Thisseth is a concept of Torugun, the idea of a boundary that can be struck into being at the edge of the Three Futures, where the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old oaths between the cities, Thisseth was invoked to cut a clean line through disputed ground. It is remembered as a principle more than a body, felt where a decision hardens into fact.
